templates.name: Pull request review
templates.line: Reviews pull requests you’re asked to review and lists risky changes.
templates.firstChat: Asks which repos to cover, then reviews the open pull requests waiting on your review and posts its findings here, with file and line. It doesn’t comment on GitHub until you say it can.
templates.watches: Pull requests waiting on your review, in the repos you pick
templates.does: Reviews each one and lists risky changes and missing tests, with file and line.
templates.reports: Here, when a review is requested
example: #4121: the retry counter is never reset, so a second outage stops retries.
No test covers the new timeout path.

templates.name: Bug investigation
templates.line: Reproduces a reported bug and finds where it starts.
templates.firstChat: Give it a bug report or an issue link. It starts an agent in a new workspace that writes down how to reproduce it, then reports the cause. It writes a fix only after you agree.
templates.watches: Bug reports you hand it, and Linear issues assigned to you
templates.does: Reproduces the bug in a new workspace, finds where it starts, and proposes a fix.
templates.reports: Here, when it has a repro and a cause
example: Reproduced ORC-640 on Windows: paste drops the last line when it has no newline.
Cause: the paste end marker goes out before the final chunk. Start a fix?

templates.name: Dependency updates
templates.line: Checks for outdated and vulnerable packages and proposes upgrades.
templates.firstChat: Lists outdated and vulnerable packages in a repo you pick, most urgent first. After you agree, an agent opens one pull request per group.
templates.watches: Packages in the repos you pick
templates.does: Lists advisories and outdated packages, most urgent first; upgrades one group per pull request once agreed.
example: 1 advisory: http-client 6.19 has a high-severity fix in 6.21.
4 minor upgrades can go in one pull request.

templates.name: Unreviewed agent work
templates.line: A daily list of finished agent work nobody has looked at yet.
templates.firstChat: Lists workspaces whose agent finished with changes you haven’t reviewed or turned into a pull request. Orca already tells you when an agent is waiting on you; this covers what’s done.
templates.watches: Your Orca workspaces
templates.does: Lists workspaces whose agent finished with changes nobody reviewed or opened a pull request for.
example: mobile-pairing finished yesterday with a 340-line diff, no pull request.
2 more finished this week.

templates.name: Workspace cleanup
templates.line: Finds finished or abandoned workspaces and offers to remove them.
templates.firstChat: Lists workspaces whose pull request merged or that haven’t changed in two weeks, with any uncommitted changes. It removes only the ones you pick.
templates.watches: Your Orca workspaces and their pull requests
templates.does: Lists workspaces that are done or abandoned, with uncommitted changes; removes only the ones you pick.
example: 6 workspaces are done: their pull requests merged this week.
2 folders haven’t changed since Oct 20.

templates.name: Security check
templates.line: Looks at merged changes for leaked secrets and risky code.
templates.firstChat: Reviews last week’s merged pull requests in a repo you pick and lists anything that needs a second look, with file and line.
templates.watches: Merged pull requests in the repos you pick
templates.does: Checks them for leaked secrets, injection, missing auth and unsafe defaults.
templates.reports: Here, Mondays at 9 AM and when a pull request merges
example: #4133 logs the full request headers, including the auth token.
Nothing else this week.

templates.name: Release readiness
templates.line: Tracks what’s blocking the next release.
templates.firstChat: Keeps a short readiness list: failing checks, pull requests waiting for review, open blockers.
templates.watches: Pull requests, checks and workspaces
templates.does: Keeps a short readiness list: failing checks, pull requests waiting for review, open blockers.
example: 1.5 is blocked by one failing check: typecheck on #4121.
Two pull requests still need a review: #4108, #4130.

templates.name: Release notes
templates.line: Drafts the next release’s notes from merged pull requests.
templates.firstChat: Finds the last release tag and drafts notes in three groups: new, fixed, changed. You edit them here.
templates.watches: Pull requests merged since the last release
templates.does: Drafts release notes for users in three groups: new, fixed, changed.
example: Draft for 1.5: 4 new, 9 fixed, 2 changed.
Biggest change: bots can share skills.

templates.name: CI failures
templates.line: Explains failed checks and keeps a list of flaky ones.
templates.firstChat: Reads the last two weeks of check runs and lists the flaky ones, then explains each failing check on your open pull requests. It starts a fix only after you agree.
templates.watches: Check runs in the repos you pick
templates.does: Tells flaky checks from real failures, explains each failure, and keeps a list of flaky checks.
templates.reports: Here, Mondays at 9 AM and when a check fails
templates.needsSetup: GitHub can’t filter failures by branch yet, so the bot looks at every failure in the repo and skips the ones that don’t matter. Each one costs a turn.
example: #4130 typecheck: a renamed export, two call sites missed. Fix is one commit.
Flakiest this week: terminal-resize test, 4 of 30 runs.

templates.name: Deploy watch
templates.line: Posts what changed in each deploy and flags failed ones.
templates.firstChat: Gives you an automation address for your deploy tool to call, then summarizes each deploy from the pull requests it shipped.
templates.watches: Calls from your deploy tool
templates.does: Summarizes each deploy from the pull requests it shipped, and flags failed ones.
templates.needsSetup: No deploy-tool connector: you add the automation’s address to your deploy tool by hand.
example: Production deploy 14:02: 5 pull requests, including the relay retry fix.
Staging deploy failed at migrate: column already exists.

templates.name: Support triage
templates.line: Keeps a list of questions nobody has answered.
templates.firstChat: Lists unanswered questions in the Slack channels you pick, with links, and notes which already have an issue.
templates.watches: Slack channels you pick
templates.does: Lists unanswered questions with links, and notes which already have a Linear issue.

schedules.when: Weekdays, every 2 hours from 9 AM to 5 PM

example: 3 new questions in #help since 11 AM. Oldest: SSH remote keeps disconnecting, 2 hours.
“Can I export a bot?” already has SUP-212.

templates.name: Feedback digest
templates.line: Turns feedback into a weekly list of themes.
templates.firstChat: Groups the last month of feedback in the channels you pick into themes, with counts and quotes.
templates.watches: Slack feedback channels
templates.does: Groups feedback into themes with quotes and counts, and links existing Linear issues.
example: Top theme: pasting in the Windows terminal, 7 people, linked ORC-640.
New this week: 3 people asked to export a bot.

templates.name: Bug report intake
templates.line: Turns bug reports in Slack into tracked issues with repro steps.
templates.firstChat: Reads the channel you pick and drafts an issue for each new bug report. It files them only after you approve.
templates.watches: The Slack channel where bugs are reported
templates.does: Drafts a Linear issue with repro steps for each bug report; files it once approved.
templates.reports: Here, when a bug is reported
example: Drafted: “Terminal freezes after sleep on macOS 27”, steps from the thread.
Possible duplicate of ORC-702.

templates.name: GitHub issue triage
templates.line: Labels new issues, finds duplicates and asks for missing details.
templates.firstChat: Goes through the last week of new issues in a repo you pick and proposes labels and duplicates here.
templates.watches: New issues in the repos you pick
templates.does: Proposes labels and duplicates, and lists missing details, for each new issue.
templates.reports: Here, when an issue is opened
example: #2210: bug, windows, duplicate of #2188.
#2214 has no version or steps. Ask for them?

templates.name: Project briefing
templates.line: A weekly brief on the projects you pick.
templates.firstChat: Writes what changed, what’s blocked and what needs a decision for the projects you pick.
templates.watches: Linear projects and GitHub repos
templates.does: Writes what changed, what’s blocked and what needs a decision.
example: Mobile v2: 6 issues closed, 2 waiting on design.
Needs a decision: ORC-902, push permission copy.

templates.name: Docs upkeep
templates.line: Flags docs that no longer match merged code.
templates.firstChat: Reads last week’s merged pull requests and lists docs pages that now say something wrong.
templates.watches: Merged pull requests and the docs in the repos you pick
templates.does: Lists docs pages that no longer match what merged, with the line that is now wrong.
example: docs/remote.md still says SSH needs a restart; #4108 removed that.
1 more page mentions the old setting name.

templates.name: Spec drafting
templates.line: Turns a discussion into a short spec you can share.
templates.firstChat: Give it a Slack thread or a doc. It drafts a one-page spec and asks about anything left open.
templates.watches: Slack threads and docs you hand it
templates.does: Drafts a one-page spec: problem, decision, scope, open questions.
example: Draft: “Bot sharing v2”. 3 decisions, 2 open questions.
Saved to your Drive as a doc.

templates.name: Backlog cleanup
templates.line: Finds stale, duplicate and unowned issues.
templates.firstChat: Lists issues untouched for 60 days, likely duplicates and issues with no owner, for a team you pick.
templates.watches: Linear issues for the team you pick
templates.does: Lists stale issues, likely duplicates and issues with no owner.
templates.reports: Here, on the 1st of each month
example: 14 issues untouched since August.
ORC-511 and ORC-688 look like the same bug.

templates.name: Incident notes
templates.line: Keeps a timeline in an incident channel and drafts the write-up.
templates.firstChat: Follows the incident channel you pick and its threads, keeps a timestamped timeline, and drafts a blameless write-up when it’s over.
templates.watches: The incident channel you pick, and its threads
templates.does: Keeps a timestamped timeline, then drafts a blameless write-up.
templates.reports: Here, during and after an incident
example: 14:02 alert fired; 14:09 rollback started; 14:21 errors back to normal.
Write-up draft ready.

templates.name: On-call handoff
templates.line: A weekly summary of alerts, incidents and open follow-ups.
templates.firstChat: Reads your alert channel and incident issues from the past week and writes the handoff.
templates.watches: Your alert channel and incident issues
templates.does: Summarizes the week’s alerts and incidents, and lists open follow-ups.
templates.needsSetup: No paging-tool connector: it reads alerts only where they’re posted in Slack.
example: 12 alerts, 2 incidents. Disk alert on cell-3 fired 5 times.
3 follow-ups still open.

templates.name: Replies you owe
templates.line: Reminds you of replies you still owe.
templates.firstChat: Finds questions to you with no reply, and things you said you’d do, in Slack threads and issue comments.
templates.watches: Slack threads and Linear comments
templates.does: Finds questions to you with no reply, and things you said you’d do.
example: You told a teammate “I’ll check tomorrow” in #design, 2 days ago.
ORC-881 has a question for you from yesterday.

templates.name: Daily standup notes
templates.line: What you and your agents did yesterday, and what’s next.
templates.firstChat: Writes yesterday’s notes from your workspaces, merged pull requests and moved issues. You copy them where your team reads them.
templates.watches: Your workspaces, pull requests and issues
templates.does: Writes yesterday’s notes and today’s plan.
example: Yesterday: merged #4121, relay retry. Agents finished 2 workspaces.
Today: ORC-702, review #4130.

templates.name: Email digest
templates.line: Twice a day, the emails that need a reply from you.
templates.firstChat: Reads today’s inbox and lists emails that need your reply, newest first. It never sends email.
templates.watches: Your inbox
templates.does: Lists emails that need a reply from you, newest first. Never sends email.
templates.reports: Here, weekdays at 9 AM and 2 PM
example: 2 need a reply: the security review date, and an invoice question.
14 newsletters skipped.

templates.name: Meeting prep
templates.line: Before each meeting, the issues, pull requests and docs it’s about.
templates.firstChat: Looks at today’s calendar and writes a short prep note for each meeting.
templates.watches: Your calendar
templates.does: Before each meeting, lists the issues, pull requests and docs it is about.
example: Mobile sync at 11: ORC-902 needs a decision; #4130 is waiting on you.
Doc: “Push permission copy”.
